WRITTEN WARNING / CORRECTIVE ACTION NOTICE
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

DESCRIPTION OF THE ISSUE
This notice documents a concern with Jordan Lee's performance or conduct.

Description of the issue:
_______________________________________________
_______________________________________________

Prior discussion, if any: _______________________________________________

EXPECTATIONS GOING FORWARD
Acme, Inc. expects Jordan Lee to address the concern described above going forward. Continued or related issues may lead to further corrective action, up to and including termination of employment.

AT-WILL EMPLOYMENT
Your employment with Acme, Inc. is at-will, meaning either you or the Company may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause or notice.

[Verified — checked 2026-08-29]
  "in the absence of distinguishing features or provisions, or a consideration in addition to the services to be rendered, contracts for life or permanent employment are indefinite hirings terminable at the will of either party."
  — Toussaint v. Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Michigan, 408 Mich. 579 (1980) (https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/2222573/toussaint-v-blue-cross-blue-shield/)
  "Blue Cross had established a company policy to discharge for just cause only ... and thereby had committed itself to discharge him only for just cause ... There were, thus, on this separate basis alone, special circumstances sufficient to overcome the presumptive construction that the contract was terminable at will."
  — Toussaint v. Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Michigan, 408 Mich. 579 (1980) (https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/2222573/toussaint-v-blue-cross-blue-shield/)
  "the disclaimer was contained within a welcoming section of the employee handbook rather than in a separate provision where a reasonable person ought to have noticed it"
  — Lincoln v. Wackenhut Corp., 867 P.2d 701 (Wyo. 1994) (https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/1196517/lincoln-v-wackenhut-corp/)
  Known gap: The general rule stated here is correct as a default, but it is a default, not an absolute: an employer's own policy statements — a handbook provision promising discharge only "for cause," for example — can override it, unless an effective disclaimer preserves at-will status. Whether a disclaimer is effective turns on how conspicuous it is: courts have specifically held that a disclaimer buried inside a handbook's welcoming section, rather than set off in its own prominent provision, can be insufficient. This clause is reused across several documents in this corpus; wherever it appears alongside a separate welcome or introductory section in the same document, that section is worth checking against this exact issue — a disclaimer tucked into a greeting rather than given its own prominent place is a real, checkable structural risk, not just a hypothetical one.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Please sign below to acknowledge that you have received and reviewed this notice. Signing doesn't necessarily mean you agree with it.

Employee: Jordan Lee
Date: _______________

—
